candidate.title: Duplex Sequencing
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina Duplex Sequencing schematic: rare-variant-bearing duplex DNA, alpha/beta adaptors with P5/P7 arms and random 12 bp molecular indices, combined ligation/PCR library generation, sequencing, per-tag single-strand consensus, and complementary-strand integration to a rare-variant-retaining duplex consensus. The mutation overview is context, not a mutation-generating operation. One representative read-family stack stands for per-tag processing of both original strands. The terminal product is sequence data, not a newly synthesized rare-variant molecule. No alternative workflow is depicted; catalogue product names and unshown capture, single-nucleus, RNA, and mtDNA-specific preparations do not expand the target scope.

states.label: Original double-stranded DNA containing a rare variant
features: The biological target is a rare DNA sequence variant, represented by matching orange marks at the corresponding position on both complementary strands.
The far-left yellow highlight and gray marker locate the rare mutation in the overview; no capture, mutation induction, or fragmentation operation is depicted.

evidence.locator: Left input duplex: two blue lines with orange marks; "A mutation occurs on both strands"
Far-left overview: "Very rare mutation" and explanatory caption about sequencing and aligning both DNA strands
Abstract, independent tagging and sequencing of both strands
evidence.quote: This approach greatly reduces errors by independently tagging and sequencing each of the two strands of a DNA duplex. As the two strands are complementary, true mutations are found at the same position in both strands.

states.label: Alpha/beta molecular-tagging adaptors with P5/P7 arms
features: Y-shaped adaptors are labeled alpha at the left end and beta at the right end; each is labeled "12 random base index".
Left adaptor: orange upper arm P5 and green lower arm P7. Right adaptor: green upper arm P7 and orange lower arm P5.
Primer sequences and random 12 bp indices are carried by the adaptors; the diagram does not specify chemical end groups or a ligation enzyme.

operations.label: Ligate and PCR
operations.description: Ligate the molecular-tagging adaptors to the DNA template and PCR-amplify the tagged template, yielding the DNA library for sequencing. The diagram combines these changes in one block.
operations.mechanism: Adaptor ligation followed by PCR, at the level explicitly stated by the figure and catalogue description.
operations.information_effect: Covalently carried adaptor tags and primer identities allow amplified copies to be associated with their original DNA strand and the two strands to be related to one original duplex; PCR supplies repeated observations of that target.

operations.label: Sequence
operations.description: Sequence the amplified tagged DNA library to obtain repeated insert-sequence observations associated with molecular tags and strand identity. The output records the two original-strand family populations separately for consensus processing.
operations.mechanism: Deep DNA sequencing; no read lengths, sequencing-cycle design, or alignment settings are specified in the schematic.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the DNA insert and molecular-identity information to sequence data. A single sequencing interface produces the two strand-derived data branches, with true-variant signal and possible technical errors.

method_scopes.rationale: The card heading and method-specific Schmitt 2012 citation identify the sole target as Duplex Sequencing. All recorded operations apply to this schematic-level tagged-duplex implementation. The two SSCS records are independent local instances for the complementary original strands under one every-tag caption; sequencing is a shared readout and duplex consensus is the genuine two-input integration. Alpha/beta denote the two depicted end adaptors and are not asserted to be names for the original DNA strands. This resolves the drawn route without claiming that every broader family implementation has the same complete preparation.
